narrative:
The model determined that you have an 81% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This high likelihood led directly to the denial of your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. While only 12.6% of approved applicants are in this situation, the model sees an overdrawn account as a clear warning sign that strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

Your credit history of having no prior credits or all paid also worked against you. This is quite rare—only 1% of approved applicants fall into this category—and it further increased the model's concern about your reliability.

The fact that you are requesting the loan to buy a new car added some additional negative pressure, though it had less impact than the first two factors. While new-car loans are fairly common among approved applicants (16.5%), the model still viewed this purpose as tilting the odds slightly against approval in your specific case.

To improve your chances next time, focus first on bringing your checking account balance positive and building a track record of on-time credit payments. Once those areas look stronger, reapply. Many people in similar situations have successfully turned their applications around by addressing these core financial signals. (218 words)
